g.text: Message / resume segment or interrupt target.
Never resolve the latest active execution on every event.
Control bindings can refer to executions on another instance.
Fixed root user event and internal resume-segment cursor.
No raw credentials or public execution identifier.
Only original user event references are public.
All writers share causal prerequisite checks and ordered commit.
Message admission locks the Session and rechecks idle in the DB.
Append the message and set running together; reject new messages while busy.
Interrupt event and stop intent commit together for a fixed target.
Confirmations atomically claim the one pending tool; stop wins if committed first.
Terminal event and target result link also commit atomically.
Allocate sequence and append atomically, retaining lock to commit.
Network and model/tool work stay outside the transaction.
Implementation names and scheduling remain target-only.
Receipt first, exactly once; then matching output.
Slow clients fail independently without cancelling execution.
DTOs never cross the HTTP response boundary.
fixed target, not a remote Java object
